 Exhibit 99.1 | Press Release | Sanofi to acquire Insmed in strategic step that strengthens long-term future 
 | 
 • | Insmed is a transformative acquisition providing strong strategic fit that complements Sanofi’s immunology
and rare disease portfolio | • | Sanofi will gain access to two
 first-in-disease commercialized products and pipeline assets, strengthening its mid-to long-term growth outlook and its position
in Respiratory | • | Sanofi will pay $175 per share, for a total consideration of $41.0 billion / €37.6 billion in
cash. The transaction is expected to be EPS accretive by the end of 2028 | • | Sanofi retains appropriate capacity to invest in early-stage BD/M&A opportunities. Sanofi confirms its
progressive dividend policy and expects to maintain a strong credit rating post transaction 
 | 
 Paris, November 24,
2026 . Sanofi today announced an agreement to acquire Insmed Incorporated (Insmed), a publicly traded, US-based global biopharmaceutical company with two commercialized medicines and a promising, innovative
pipeline. The transaction is intended to broaden Sanofi’s presence in respiratory diseases, where significant unmet patient need remains. 
 The
acquisition includes Brinsupri (brensocatib) and Arikayce (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), along with a differentiated, phase 3 clinical program, treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP), which has potential across multiple rare
respiratory diseases. The acquisition also brings promising earlier-stage programs and research capabilities across immunology and rare diseases, reinforcing Sanofi’s own innovation and immunology capabilities globally. 
 Insmed is a compelling strategic fit, building on Sanofi’s longstanding experience in immunology and rare diseases. Combining Insmed’s highly
differentiated portfolio and scientific expertise with Sanofi’s global reach is expected to expand patient access to important respiratory medicines while augmenting Sanofi’s commercial leadership and the rebuild of its pipeline. 
 This acquisition is expected to improve Sanofi’s financial profile over the mid- and long-term and expand
the company’s portfolio in core focus areas. 
 “I am delighted to welcome Insmed to Sanofi. This acquisition is a major
strategic step to significantly accelerate our mid- and long-term growth trajectory and further strengthen our mid- and early-stage pipeline,” said Belen
Garijo , Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi. “Insmed builds on our already successful presence in respiratory diseases through its highly differentiated portfolio, strong science and proven commercial success. Together, we have the
opportunity to build on these achievements, reach more patients globally and reinforce our leadership in diseases of significant unmet medical need. This acquisition is another example of how we are executing on our strategic roadmap with momentum
to drive Sanofi’s next phase of growth.” 
 “The Insmed team has always set out to change what is possible for
patients. In just over a year since launch, we made Brinsupri the standard of care for NCFB patients, while continuing to advance our commercial portfolio and phase 3 pipeline with a combined multibillion-dollar peak sales potential,” said
 Will Lewis , Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Insmed. “This transaction delivers immediate, certain cash value for Insmed shareholders and ensures the momentum we have built continues. In Sanofi we have a partner that
recognizes the value of our science, commercial execution, and the exceptional culture we have created. Together, we expect to bring our therapies to more patients around the world, faster than we ever could on our own.” | 1/ | 
 Brinsupri is a small molecule, once-daily, oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1),
approved in the US, EU, UK and Japan for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), with the indicated patient populations varying by jurisdiction. Brinsupri is the first and only approved treatment for NCFB
and a first-in-class DPP1 inhibitor targeting neutrophilic inflammation. Following its US launch in August 2025, Brinsupri has already reached blockbuster status,
delivering $1.09 billion in revenue through September 30, 2026, with substantial additional growth expected. 
 Arikayce is an inhaled
antibacterial treatment used in combination with multidrug therapy for certain adults with mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease and is the only approved inhaled therapy specifically indicated for treatment-refractory patients in the US, EU
and Japan. Arikayce revenues were $433.8 million in 2025, representing 19% annual growth. In addition, the US Food and Drug Administration in September accepted under priority review an application for Arikayce for the treatment of MAC lung
disease as part of a combination antibacterial drug regimen. 
 TPIP is a prostanoid being developed as a once-daily inhaled therapy for pulmonary
hypertension and fibrotic lung disease. With once-daily dosing and the potential for multiple rare respiratory indications, TPIP could become a significant growth driver for Sanofi beyond 2030, subject to successful clinical development, regulatory
approvals, and commercial execution. 
 Transaction terms and financial considerations 
 Under the terms of the merger agreement, Sanofi will acquire all outstanding shares of Insmed for $175 per share in cash, reflecting a total equity value of
approximately $41.0 billion/ €37.6 billion. 
 The transaction is expected to strengthen Sanofi’s
 mid- to long-term growth profile. The transaction is expected to be accretive to Sanofi’s business earnings per share (EPS) by the end of 2028. 
 Sanofi is funding the acquisition through a combination of debt financing and cash on hand, and has secured committed financing in support of the transaction.
Sanofi will maintain its conservative financial policy. The combined group’s anticipated cash generation is expected to support rapid deleveraging, while retaining flexibility to invest in early-stage BD/M&A opportunities. Sanofi remains
committed to its capital allocation policy, including its progressive dividend, and expects to maintain a strong credit rating. 
 The transaction has been
approved by the boards of directors of both companies. 
 The closing of the transaction is subject to approval by Insmed shareholders, receipt of U.S. and
certain non-U.S. regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. 
 Subject to the satisfaction or waiver of
these conditions, the transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. 
 The proposed acquisition is not expected to have any impact on
Sanofi’s financial guidance for 2026. 
 Conference call for investors and analysts 
 Sanofi will host a conference call and webcast for investors and analysts at 1400 CET/8 a.m. ET today. The presentation will be available on the Investor
Relations section of sanofi.com before the call starts. | 2/ | 
 Please register here: 
 https://sanofi.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_utrSGRoUSfSjQtkCADrT_g 
 About Brinsupri 
 Brinsupri (brensocatib) is a small
molecule, once-daily, oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1), designed to inhibit the activation of neutrophil serine proteases that are key drivers of chronic airway inflammation in NCFB. 
 In the US and Japan, Brinsupri is approved for the treatment of NCFB in adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older. In the EU and UK, it is
approved for patients with NCFB aged 12 years and older with two or more exacerbations in the prior 12 months. 
 NCFB is a serious, chronic progressive
lung disease in which airways are permanently widened, causing ongoing productive cough and exacerbations. Insmed estimates that approximately 500,000 patients in the US, 600,000 in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK combined, and 150,000 in
Japan are diagnosed with NCFB. These estimates describe diagnosed patient populations, and some of these patients in the different jurisdictions are eligible for Brinsupri under its current labels. 
 Brinsupri is associated with dermatologic adverse reactions, including rash, dry skin and hyperkeratosis, and with gingival and periodontal adverse reactions.
Patients should be monitored for new skin conditions and receive regular dental care. Live attenuated vaccines should be avoided during treatment. 
 About Arikayce 
 Arikayce (amikacin liposome inhalation
suspension) is a novel, inhaled, once-daily liposomal formulation of amikacin, approved in the US, EU and Japan. 
 In the US, it is indicated as part of a
combination antibacterial regimen for adults with limited or no alternative treatment options who have MAC lung disease and have not achieved negative sputum cultures after at least six consecutive months of a multidrug background regimen. Its US
indication was approved under the accelerated approval pathway on the basis of sputum culture conversion. Clinical benefit has not yet been established, and continued approval may depend on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory studies.
Arikayce was approved by FDA using the limited population pathway. This means FDA has approved this medicine for a limited and specific patient population, and studies on the medicine may have only answered focused questions about its safety and
effectiveness. 
 MAC lung disease is a rare and often chronic infection that can cause irreversible lung damage; Insmed estimates that 95,000 to 115,000
patients in the US have diagnosed MAC lung disease. These estimates describe diagnosed patient populations, not the populations eligible for Arikayce under its current labels. 
 Arikayce carries a US boxed warning for increased respiratory adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and
exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease, which have led to hospitalization in some patients. 
 About TPIP 
 TPIP is a dry powder formulation of treprostinil palmitil, a treprostinil prodrug. It is being developed for once-daily administration. Its phase 3 program
includes PALM-PAH in pulmonary arterial hypertension, PALM-ILD in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, and
 PALM-PPF in progressive pulmonary fibrosis. A phase 3 study in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is planned to start in the first half of 2027. 
 TPIP is not approved for any indication in any jurisdiction. Its safety and efficacy have not been established. | 3/ | 
 About Sanofi 
 Sanofi is an R&D driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering
compelling growth. We apply our deep understanding of the immune system to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world, with an innovative pipeline that could benefit millions more. Our team is
guided by one purpose: we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives; this inspires us to drive progress and deliver positive impact for our people and the communities we serve, by addressing the most urgent healthcare,
environmental, and societal challenges of our time. 
 Sanofi is listed on EURONEXT: SAN and NASDAQ: SNY 
 About Insmed 
 Insmed is a people-first global
biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases. The Company is advancing a
diverse portfolio of approved and mid- to late-stage investigational medicines — including two approved therapies to treat chronic, debilitating lung diseases — as well as cutting-edge drug
discovery focused on serving patient communities where the need is greatest. Insmed’s commercial portfolio and clinical pipeline are organized around three therapeutic areas: Respiratory, Immunology & Inflammation, and
Neuro & Other Rare. The Company’s research engine is advancing a wide range of technologies and modalities, including gene therapy, AI-driven protein engineering, RNA end-joining, and synthetic rescue, in the pursuit of future pipeline candidates. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, Insmed has offices and research locations throughout the United States, Europe, and Japan.
Visit www.Insmed.com to learn more or follow the Company on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube , and X .
